results.title: Old Knobbley
results.overview: In 17th century England, two women persecuted for witchcraft find sanctuary and safety at the site of a five-hundred year old oak tree.

results.title: Á Huldu - The Hidden Ones
results.overview: In the Icelandic countryside, a news cameraman is found dead under unsettling circumstances, his reporter colleague has vanished without a trace.  The mystery remains unsolved.  Years later, a documentary crew retraces the investigation, piecing together fragments of testimony, archival material, and newly uncovered footage. What begins as a cold case review becomes something more elusive as new evidence reveals hidden connections and unanswered questions.  Á Huldu – The Hidden Ones is an 85-minute English and Icelandic-language feature that adopts a true-crime documentary framework to explore the instability of truth, the ethics of observation, and the persistence of unresolved narratives.

results.title: A Joke
results.overview: Xiao Mei and Xiao Shuai turn their marriage bed into a battleground. The two formidable rivals bring all they know to the game, locked in a romantic contest. As their emotional tug-of-war unfolds to a final reckoning, both come face to face with their true selves.

results.title: Spikes
results.overview: Three childhood friends from a remote village decide to flee their homes and hitchhike toward a costume rave party in the South. Over a three-day journey set against the diverse landscape, they face a series of encounters that accelerate the hidden tensions between them. As the road unfolds, their lifelong, unquestioned bond begins to fracture, and their friendship is pushed to a point of no return.

results.title: We Still Have Time
results.overview: One weekend, a man receives a phone call that forces him to take his son on a special "visit".

results.title: Tao
results.overview: Jinzi wins a huge cash prize, yet loses everything in the process.

results.title: See
results.overview: Drawing on the lives of three wanderers, the film explores the delicate balance between the self and life, offering viewers at every stage of life an answer that belongs only to them.

results.title: A Season
results.overview: Watching Shehuo, we see not a millennium-old relic, but a living life spanning a thousand years. Through all bleakness lies our dream; across a long wandering journey lies our homecoming.

results.title: Dolphins: My Close Encounters
results.overview: Swiss marine biologist Angela Ziltener has been diving with wild dolphins in the Red Sea for over 15 years. What began as a scientific study evolved into a deeply personal journey. As she found herself becoming increasingly immersed in the world of dolphins, Angela was confronted with a more profound question: Who was actually observing whom here?

results.title: Erinner mich an morgen
results.overview: Geriatric carer Lea loves her job and uses imaginative role-plays to help her patients bring lost moments back to life. When the unusually young patient Hedda arrives and Lea is reminded of her own mother, she begins to overstep professional boundaries. What starts out as particular closeness and empathy, develops into a reality created by Lea herself, in which past and present, care and personal need, role and identity become inextricably interwoven.

results.title: Deep Home Front
results.overview: Deep Home Front tells the story of the Kama region during the Great Patriotic War. Far from the front lines, people worked to the limits of their endurance, raised children, mourned loved ones, and believed that their labor was itself another front in the war. The film focuses on everyday life on the home front, where people sacrificed their health and, in some cases, were forced to live in circus arenas and orchestra pits. Teenage girls worked as blasters in the potash mines, laboratory assistants tested a typhus vaccine using methods unimaginable today, and more than 2000 housewives became record-breaking coal miners. These are only a few of the remarkable stories uncovered by the filmmakers. The screenplay is based on extensive research in state archives, departmental and municipal museums, and libraries. The production team also recorded dozens of interviews, while the film incorporates more than one hundred documented eyewitness accounts from the wartime years.

results.title: Letuni
results.overview: “Up, flyers! Everyone to the runway!” These are the commands that begin each morning in the Abdulaev family. Former military pilot Samizhon teaches his children never to lie, yet for many years he has kept one important chapter of his life from them.

results.title: BARI
results.overview: Seeking to bring the dead back to life, Bari ventures into the underworld in pursuit of a life-giving flower. Yet her journey is driven not by heroic sacrifice, but by an escalating and uncontrollable obsession. She enters an eerie realm where life and death coexist on a horizontal plane, and as her desire consumes her, she is forced to confront the impossibility of fulfilling it. Trapped in an endless cycle of longing and loss, Bari can do nothing but repeat her journey.

results.title: Fireflies
results.overview: In the blue hour between day and night, a quiet neighborhood is visited by fireflies and ghostly lights.

results.title: Where is Ava?
results.overview: To protect themselves from a mysterious phenomenon that turns women into men, a family retreats to an alpine chalet. Their desire to preserve the female sex within the family leads them down a path of radicalization. The descent into inhumanity unfolds almost imperceptibly, and patterns of behavior long thought to be outgrown resurface. Better able to cope with protogyny, the children offer a small glimmer of hope.

results.title: Lucky Star
results.overview: Struggling actor, Lucky, spends his gap year embarrassing himself and attempting to be the next big star of Hollywood.

results.title: Descontinuados
results.overview: A film about the human relation with artificial intelligence.

results.title: The Flesh of the Mountain
results.overview: The ragged, desolate landscapes around eastern California’s Owens Lake are rendered in negative monochrome in the latest entry in Adam Piron’s film cycle about the brutal history of Indigenous land expropriation in the American West. Deploying images from Thomas Edison’s 1894 films of Buffalo Bill’s Wild West Show, The Flesh of the Mountain recounts the violent legacy of white settlers’ claim upon Paiute lands for the mining of silver—an essential component of motion-picture film.
